claims.text: The target materials are single-phase, chemically random, disordered high-entropy alloys intended for thermal insulation.
A multi-fidelity machine-learning framework can integrate ab initio phonon-transport calculations with experimental inelastic-scattering data.
The integrated framework will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than conventional prediction methods.
Ab initio molecular dynamics, machine-learned force fields, and Green–Kubo calculations can be used to derive thermal conductivity.
Inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering can experimentally characterize phonon dynamics in an HEA.
Strong chemical disorder in HEAs produces mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations reduce phonon lifetimes.
Disorder-induced lattice distortion enhances phonon scattering and lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Quantitatively capturing disorder-driven phonon scattering will improve prediction of HEA lattice thermal conductivity.
Conventional models inadequately account for multicomponent phonon-scattering effects and do not exploit inelastic-scattering data.
The integrated approach may reduce prediction error by approximately 15–20% relative to current models.
The framework's accuracy advantage applies across approximately 300–700 K.
The framework's improved accuracy is limited to chemically disordered, single-phase HEAs.
The framework may not generalize to ordered or partially ordered alloys.
The framework may not generalize when scattering mechanisms other than mass and force-constant fluctuations dominate.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant prediction-error reduction of roughly 15–20%, or failure to observe the predicted low conductivity, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention presents Green–Kubo as a calculation-based component of the predictive framework, whereas the experimental design describes Green–Kubo as an example of a direct thermal-conductivity measurement. These are inconsistent methodological characterizations.
